title: Conserving Animal Feed: Hay
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Make hay from grass or maize stover in a box baler (a wooden box with open ends and strings laid across it) and build a small stack on a raised base. Talk about the last drought and what happened to animals.

skills.key_step: The child describes methods of conserving forage for drought (haymaking by baling or stacking, standing forage, crop residues) and says why: feed when grass is gone, fewer animal deaths, milk and income kept.

floor.prerequisite: Knows why produce is dried to keep.
floor.question: Why does dried food keep?

representations: pictures of bales, stacks and a paddock
steps: Plenty in the rains, little in the drought.
Conserve: bale, stack, keep standing forage, keep stover.

board.do: Draw a calendar with green months and brown months.

misconceptions.ask: When should forage be conserved for a drought?
misconceptions.repair: Show a calendar: grass is plenty in April and gone in September.

listen_for: Grass cut and stood in heaps
misconceptions.repair: Show a fenced paddock left ungrazed in the rains.

listen_for: Burn it to clear the shamba
misconceptions.ask: What can be done with maize stover after harvest to help in a drought?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what cattle eat when the grass is gone.

misconceptions.ask: Why is conserving feed better than moving animals in a drought?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss the losses of animals in the last drought.

checks.question: Name two methods of conserving forage.
checks.answer: any two of baling, stacking, standing forage, keeping stover

checks.question: Why conserve forage?
checks.answer: to feed animals in a drought

skills.key_step: The child says how hay is made: cut at flowering, dry and turn until dry but green, bale in a box baler or stack on a raised base with a sloping top, cover, store dry, feed in the dry season.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the methods of conserving forage.
floor.question: Name a method.

steps: Bale or stack on a raised base.

board.do: Draw a stack on the ground with a flat top.
Ask what happens in the rain.
Wait for "it gets wet and rots".
Redraw it raised with a sloping top.

listen_for: When it is old, dry and brown
misconceptions.ask: When is grass best cut for hay?
misconceptions.repair: Compare green leafy grass and old brown stems: which would a cow choose?

misconceptions.ask: Where are hay bales kept after baling?
misconceptions.repair: Show a bale left out in rain: black and mouldy inside.

misconceptions.ask: What happens if hay is baled while still damp?
misconceptions.repair: Smell a damp bale left for a week.

listen_for: On the ground with a flat top
misconceptions.ask: How should a hay stack be built?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water on a flat-topped and a sloping model stack.

checks.question: When is grass cut for hay?
Why must hay be dry before baling?
